original_question: How many proteins encoded by the gene linked to mutations observed in approximately one-fourth of meningiomas have been characterized in mammals?

final_qi.question: How many proteins encoded by the gene linked to mutations observed in approximately one-fourth of meningiomas have been characterized in mammals?
final_qi.long_answer: The gene in question is NF2, mutations of which are found in roughly 25 % of sporadic meningiomas. In mammals the NF2 gene is expressed as two distinct, well-characterised protein isoforms of the tumour-suppressor merlin/schwannomin, generated by alternative splicing of the NF2 transcript.

0.question: Which gene is linked to mutations observed in approximately one-fourth of meningiomas?

final_answer.long_answer: The tumor-suppressor gene NF2, whose loss-of-function mutations are found in roughly one-quarter of sporadic meningiomas, is alternatively spliced to generate two distinct mammalian protein products—Merlin isoform 1 and Merlin isoform 2. Thus, two proteins encoded by this gene have been characterized in mammals.
